exercises.title: English lies about vowels
exercises.body: English writes book and food with the same “oo”, but your mouth makes two different sounds. Shavian never blurs them: book is 𐑚𐑫𐑒 and food is 𐑓𐑵𐑛. When you write, stop picturing the English spelling — say the word slowly and write the vowel you actually hear.

exercises.title: Short above, long below
exercises.body: The keyboard helps you. Its two vowel rows are paired: every short vowel sits directly above its long partner — 𐑦 over 𐑰, 𐑪 over 𐑴, 𐑳 over 𐑵. If a word comes out sounding wrong, try the letter just under (or just over) the one you picked.

exercises.title: One letter, one sound
exercises.body: Watch out for English vowel pairs that are really one sound: the ai of rain is a single 𐑱, the i-e of time a single 𐑲, the o-e of home a single 𐑴. Count sounds, not letters.
